#### Protected Locations

Only a run on the host has protected locations. A run in a container has none, since nothing it mustn't touch is mounted there, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says: it isn't guarded, and its harness is given no rule against reading or editing anything.
Where the harness takes rules for what its tools may do, as Claude Code does with `--disallowedTools`, a run on the host is told what its mode keeps it off. A Code task is told it may not edit the spec location, and a Spec task the code location; the application puts back what the task changed there all the same, and says so in the task's output as a passive notice, never an error, as the [TaskTableScope](../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope) says.
It puts back only what the task itself changed: a file the task's own tool calls report writing, editing, moving, or deleting there, a subagent's included, as the referenced spec works them out, and nothing else. A file changed there while the task runs by anything else, the user copying a folder in, the editor saving, git, or another program, is the user's and is never put back, deleted, or reverted, however it changed. It puts back once, when the task is over, never while it runs, so nothing is watched and undone as it happens; and where a file the task changed was also changed by something else since, it is left as it is, the notice saying so, rather than overwriting the other change. A task that isn't running guards nothing: no location is guarded while no Code or Spec task runs on the host, and nothing the application does ever deletes a file the user put in the spec or code location, outside what `piton build` writes and owns by its manifest. A Code task is also told it may not read the spec location, alongside that, so it reads the compiled reference instead, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says. A question from the Ask tab always runs in a container, so it is never given this rule, nor any other telling it to keep off the spec location. This rule is only a nudge, and doesn't enforce anything, since a shell command can still read the files, and nothing puts anything back or stops the run when one does. A harness that takes no such rules is told nothing of either.

139:A notice is something the application tells the run's reader about the run, rather than something the harness did or a failure: chiefly that it put back changes a task made where its mode may not change anything, a Code task in the spec or a Spec task in the code. It is passive. It is never shown as an error, never in the theme's error colour, and never fails the task, changes its status, or counts among the errors a run ended with.
143:A notice is a row of its own, where it happened among the run's rows, its badge reading "Notice" with an info icon, in the muted grey of a badge that marks nothing wrong. Its output is a single line summing it up, muted, beside a right chevron, such as "Put back 3 spec files this Code task changed" or "Put back 1 code file this Spec task changed". It has no status.
147:Clicking the line expands the notice's details in place, beneath it, and its chevron turns down; clicking it again collapses them. For changes put back, the details say that a task in its mode may not change that location, so what it changed there was put back as it was, and then list each file put back, one per line, by its path in the project. A notice starts collapsed, and each stays as it was left for as long as the application runs.

Your hunch was right: Suspense was deleting the folder. While a Code task ran on the host, the guard protecting the spec checked the spec folder every half second and removed anything added there, including a folder you copied in. It now only ever puts back changes the task itself made.

- **Only the task's own changes:** a file is put back only if the task's own tool calls, or its subagents', reported writing, editing, moving or deleting it.
- **Your changes are left alone:** anything else that changes the spec while a task runs, whether you, the editor, git or another program, is never removed or reverted.
- **Once, at the end:** the put-back happens once, when the task is over, and nothing is watched or undone while it runs.
- **No overwriting:** if something else changed a file again after the task did, it's left as it is and the notice lists it under "left as they are".
- **No guard while idle:** with no Code or Spec task running on the host, nothing is guarded at all.

When the task edits the same file twice, the second edit makes it look as if something else changed the file. Such a file is left as it is and listed in the notice rather than put back. I chose that so it never risks undoing one of your changes.

The rewrite is in `src/mode_guard.rs`, with the hook that records the task's own changes in `src/prompt_mode.rs`. New tests check that a folder you copy in survives and that a file changed after the task is left alone. One existing test's fake harness now reports its write as a tool call, as a real harness does. One unrelated test, `restart_from_within_the_window_never_panics`, failed in the full run; it has passed when run on its own before.
